question: Following the local elections of 29 March 2026 in Serbia, concerns regarding electoral irregularities, an uneven playing field and incidents of violence have been raised by civil society organisations, election observers and international bodies. The Commission has also publicly acknowledged these issues and called for accountability and further electoral reforms. 1.

What concrete measures will the Commission take, within the framework of the accession process, to support and monitor the effective investigation of reported irregularities and violence, as well as the implementation of the necessary electoral reforms?

How will the Commission reflect the lack of tangible progress made in these areas in Serbia’s accession process, and what benchmarks will be used to assess whether upcoming elections, including those expected in 2027, meet EU democratic standards?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.7.2026) The Commission closely followed the local elections held on 29 March 2026 in ten municipalities in Serbia, which were observed by the Council of Europe (CoE) Congress of Local and Regional Authorities.

Following reported irregularities and incidents during the elections, including acts of violence against independent observers, citizens, representatives of political parties, and media workers, the Commission called on the competent national authorities to ensure swift and transparent follow up and to hold perpetrators accountable.

Building on the first positive steps taken to address concerns about the integrity of the electoral register, such as the adoption of the amendments to the Law on the Unified voters register and election of the audit commission, the Commission has continued to underline that the electoral process requires further tangible improvement and reform.
Priority recommendations from the CoE and the Organisation for Security Cooperation in Europe/Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights are yet to be fully implemented.

These relate to the separation of State and party, inclusiveness and comprehensiveness of the electoral reform, audit of the voter register and transparency of voter list data, greater oversight of election campaigns and their financing, and measures to enable media freedom and independence.

The Commission will continue to follow developments in the rule of law including electoral reform closely, as well as the conduct of all future elections. The proper functioning of Serbia’s democratic institutions is at the core of its EU accession process, and the Commission will report on it as part of the 2026 Enlargement Package.
